approval_required_for: Any memory-layout or runtime-ABI contract change.
Any major template replacement rather than a localized generated-integration fix.
Any repair that would alter the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper or its immutable source hashes.
Any proposed numeric-policy or tolerance change; such a change is not authorized within this repair loop.
Any SACG design-contract change that would invalidate the existing lower-layer certificate independently of a current contradictory trace.

consumes: current exact sample-project wrapper and simulation sources
current Vivado export facts and tool profile
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board simulation and all higher layers blocked. Report the exact identity, Vivado-export authority, tool-profile, or probe-binding mismatch; do not use the historical diagnosis, alter wrapper sources, bypass the checker, or patch hardware.
executable_actions.rationale: The failed interface checker reports stale source identity and unauthorized VCS compile authority, and the specialist review requires direct kernel observability. Repair the evidence binding and probe contract without changing functional RTL, the exact sample wrapper, the semantic testbench contract, or immutable comparison inputs.

consumes: immutable target checkpoint and full transformer-block tensor catalog
immutable numeric comparison policy and tolerance
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the current layer blocked and return the simulator/tool failure or missing signal set to verification-capability repair. Do not infer an RTL cause from an incomplete trace, reopen a lower layer, change tolerance, replace the target reference, or promote.
executable_actions.rationale: A current-layer direct-boundary trace is the minimum evidence needed to distinguish no kernel ingress, accepted input without completion, blocked kernel output, and completed output not propagated by the wrapper.

executable_actions.on_failure: Request one additional bounded current-layer probe for the unresolved earliest boundary. Do not select a module for repair, create a lower-layer backtrack, or promote while localization remains ambiguous.
produces: sacg_memory current-layer retry or conditional backtrack update
executable_actions.rationale: Convert the current direct trace into one bounded decision: a current-layer integration repair, an additional targeted observation, or a certificate-backed lower-layer challenge. The output-frontier symptom alone is insufficient.

consumes: exact sample-project wrapper source hash manifest
executable_actions.on_failure: Feed the new real-tool output back into current-layer CCTG localization and rerun the bounded loop. Do not promote, loosen numeric tolerance, modify golden outputs or exact wrapper sources, or reopen a lower layer unless the new trace explicitly contradicts its certificate.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute only when hierarchical_repair_decision localizes a non-architectural defect to the board wrapper integration adapter, scheduler, lifecycle propagation, data order, loader, harness, or AXI/DDR slice without contradicting the certified connected kernel. Preserve the exact sample-project wrapper hashes and all immutable semantic inputs.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep both the challenged lower layer and board layer blocked, preserve the prior certificate as challenged rather than silently discarded, and request only the missing boundary evidence. After any lower-layer repair, rerun and recertify that scope, then rerun the board layer before promotion.
produces: updated single-layer certificate or rejected challenge record
executable_actions.rationale: This action is eligible only if hierarchical_repair_decision cites a current hash-bound direct trace that contradicts a named invariant in the current single-layer certificate, including direct core start, ingress, egress, lifecycle, and causal-boundary evidence. No such contradiction is currently established.

observations: The current board layer is not promotable: case_axi_ddr_interface and functional_sim failed, while case_multilayer_functional, case_pipeline_deadlock_check, case_axi_protocol_check, case_ddr_image_roundtrip, and case_board_semantic_evidence have not run.
All supplied operator-layer and connected single-transformer-layer gates passed, and the hierarchical learning context provides a hash-validated single-layer certificate.

The conditional exact-board integration specialist review was triggered and reached the same bounded conclusion: the next required evidence is a direct read-only probe of dut.spatialacc_single_kernel ingress, egress, start, and completion.

The prior real VCS execution establishes wrapper-level progress through input completion and a ready output frontier accepting zero beats, but it does not establish whether the kernel accepted input, launched, retained tokens, asserted blocked output, or completed without propagation.

The current diagnosis projection is historical only because a live source hash changed and its gate binding is not current. It cannot authorize a repair or replay until source identity and exact Vivado export compile authority are rebound.
No supplied current trace explicitly contradicts the connected-kernel certificate; therefore reopening a leaf module or the connected kernel now would violate the hierarchical repair policy.
The present failure is a verification-capability and current-layer localization gap, not evidence of hardware functional correctness or a justified RTL replacement.
Historical SACG records must not be treated as active blockers unless sacg_memory_truth marks them active or open.
proposed_actions: Rebind the simulation identity and VCS compile authority to the current exact sample-project sources and Vivado export facts, while adding only nonintrusive direct-kernel probe configuration.

Replay the failed board transaction with the same immutable checkpoint, stimulus, reference, numeric policy, semantic contract, and wrapper hashes; collect cycle-correlated kernel ingress, egress, start, completion, valid, ready, and accepted-handshake evidence.
Use CCTG-guided localization to classify the earliest violated current-layer boundary before selecting any code repair.

If the trace localizes a wrapper, adapter, scheduler, data-order, lifecycle, or AXI/DDR integration defect without contradicting the certificate, repair only that current-layer slice and rerun all board-layer gates.

Only if the trace directly contradicts a named certified connected-kernel invariant, create a SACG backtrack request and rerun only the challenged lower-layer scope before returning to the board layer.
risks: Guessing a kernel or wrapper defect from the zero-output frontier could patch a downstream symptom while leaving the earliest violated boundary unknown.
Using the stale diagnosis or an unauthorized compile plan could produce evidence that is not bound to the current exact board sources.
Adding intrusive instrumentation or changing the sample-project wrapper could invalidate exact-wrapper hashes and lower the evidentiary value of the replay.
Reopening the connected kernel without direct core ingress, egress, lifecycle, named-boundary, and current-certificate evidence would discard valid lower-layer learning.

A board functional claim without the immutable target-model reference, full transformer-block tensor catalog, complete DUT weight-consumption proof, and frozen numeric comparison policy would be invalid.
Treating independent AXI/prefetch progress as lifecycle or output progress could mislocalize the stall.
Any repair that changes architecture, pipeline semantics, memory layout, numeric policy, tolerance, or a major template exceeds the current bounded authority.

artifacts: current Vivado export facts and authorized VCS compile plan
exact board wrapper and simulation source hash manifest
prior real VCS log showing completed wrapper ingress and zero accepted output beats
immutable full transformer-block tensor catalog and DUT weight-binding manifest
constraints: Preserve the certified operator and connected-kernel evidence unless a current hash-bound direct-boundary trace explicitly contradicts a named invariant.
Treat wrapper ingress completion and zero accepted output beats only as localization evidence, not as a hardware pass or a preselected RTL root cause.
Preserve elastic variable-latency token-pipeline semantics; enforce boundary ordering and valid-ready handshakes without requiring equal-latency stages to start or finish in the same cycle.
Keep checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference outputs, numeric policy and tolerance, semantic testbench contract, and exact board-wrapper source hashes immutable.
Expected outputs must remain target-model inference results for the same checkpoint and stimulus; random or DUT-derived expected outputs are prohibited.
DUT and weight-coverage scope is Transformer blocks only, excluding embedding, tokenization, final model norm, LM head, logits, and sampling.
Only blockers active in sacg_memory_truth are current SACG blockers; historical or superseded diagnosis records must not be reactivated.
Do not promote to backend, bitstream, or board runtime while any board-layer gate is failed or not run.
edges: dut.spatialacc_single_kernel egress -> ready board output frontier
current source identity -> exact Vivado export compile authority
immutable target-model reference -> board semantic numeric comparison

output.summary: No RTL root-cause repair or lower-layer reopening is authorized yet. The operator and connected single-transformer-layer certificates remain reusable because no current hash-bound trace contradicts a named certified invariant. First repair the current verification identity/compile-authority binding, then rerun the exact board simulation with read-only probes at dut.spatialacc_single_kernel to distinguish missing ingress, accepted-but-stalled execution, blocked egress, and completed-but-unpropagated output. Promotion remains blocked until every board-layer gate passes with real-tool and semantic evidence.
